title: Record a breaking API change at the right severity
prompt: We want to cut a release. Since the last one, the `request` helper in @acme/api was reworked to take a single options object instead of positional arguments — `request(baseUrl, path, options)` is gone, and every caller in the wild has to change. Record that in the release so it ships as the right kind of version, and tell me what version goes out.
expectation: The change removes and incompatibly modifies a public exported signature, so it is a breaking change and the release must be a major one. The agent records it as a changeset targeting `@acme/api` with a major bump (either `major`, or a configured type whose bump is major), leaves `monochange step validate` passing, and reports the resulting version. Because the three npm packages share one version group that is currently at 2.3.1, a major bump in a member takes the group to 3.0.0. The scoped id must be quoted in the changeset frontmatter.

checks.why: Release intent belongs in a file, not only in the agent's reply.

Removing a public signature is a breaking change. A minor or patch release would ship a break to consumers on a compatible version, which is the failure this scenario exists to catch. The group sits at 2.3.1, so major is the only severity that produces 3.0.0.
A changeset that does not resolve against configured ids is not release intent.
The break is in @acme/api. Recording it against the group obscures which package broke and mislabels the changelog entry.
A scoped id is not a valid YAML key unquoted; the file only parses when it is quoted.
Versions are computed from release intent; hand-editing manifests defeats the release plan and desynchronises the group.
